neighbours.label: the ' of' that introduces news someone is given or finds out (informed X of, notified X of, notice of, learned of), as opposed to ' of' after other verbs and adjectives in the same frames (accused of, thought of, tired of), and to a news verb with no ' of'
fire: The landlord notified the tenants of the sale.
The college informed its students of the fire.
The family got formal notice of the inquest this week.
By then he had learned of the accident.
Officials advised the mayor of the flood.
Staff were informed of the closure on Monday.
She first heard of the crash on the radio.
Members will get advance notice of any changes.
quiet: The landlord accused the tenants of the theft.
The college relieved its students of the fees.
The family grew tired of the inquest this week.
By then he had thought of the accident.
Officials notified the mayor by phone.
Staff were afraid of the closure on Monday.
She first spoke of the crash on the radio.
Members will get a printed copy of any changes.

short: the ' of' that introduces news someone gets
notes: Round 2. An earlier round claimed telling and learning news more widely, and failed on 'told her' (the same 1.000 before 'about' and before 'to'). ' told' is dropped here, and this round is only about ' of'. Probes: 'notice of' 0.82, 'informed patients of' 0.76, 'learned of' 0.73, 'notified residents of' 0.61; 'accused the driver of' 0.003, 'thought of' 0.10. 'reminded parents of' 0.36, on ' parents', is unclear. Other forms fired in probes and are not tested here: 'announced' 0.48, 'were told that' 0.47.
